script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'danc-parallel-modules',
  description: 'Build independent D-ANC modules in parallel: synthetic defence noise, classical baselines, adaptive filters + dual-mic simulator, Jetson deployment kit',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Build', detail: '4 module builders with unit tests' },
    { title: 'Review', detail: 'one adversarial reviewer per module, fixes applied' },
  ],
}

const ROOT = '/Users/nsivaprasadnandyala/Desktop/DRDO_Project'
const COMMON = `You are a senior audio DSP engineer building part of "D-ANC", a hybrid DNN + adaptive-filter noise-cancellation system for defence voice communications (16 kHz, real-time, Jetson AGX Orin target).
Project root: ${ROOT}. Python venv: always run "source ${ROOT}/.venv/bin/activate" before python. Package code lives in ${ROOT}/src/danc (installed editable as "danc"). Tests: "cd ${ROOT} && python -m pytest -q tests/<your test file>".
HARD RULES: never delete any file or directory (no rm, no overwriting files you did not create). Only create/edit the files assigned to you. Do not pip install anything (numpy, scipy, soundfile, soxr, librosa, pyroomacoustics, matplotlib, torch, onnxruntime, pytest are installed). Write clean, documented, production-quality code in the style of ${ROOT}/src/danc/dsp.py (read it first: it defines the shared STFT convention: fs=16000, win=320 (20 ms), hop=160 (10 ms), n_fft=320, 161 bins, sqrt-Hann; functions stft/istft (offline, aligned) and class StreamingSTFT). Cite the original algorithm papers (authors, year, venue) in docstrings; do not invent citations - if unsure of a detail, say so in a comment.
All randomness must come from a passed numpy Generator for reproducibility. Make the unit tests fast (< 60 s total) and make them pass. Finish by returning a concise summary: files created, public API (signatures), test results (paste the pytest summary line), known limitations.`

const MODULES = [
  {
    key: 'synth_noise',
    prompt: `Create ${ROOT}/src/danc/data/synth_noise.py: physically-motivated synthetic DEFENCE noise generators (we lack openly licensed recordings of gunfire/artillery/rotors/drones).
API:
  KINDS: dict[str, dict]  # kind -> {"category": "impulsive"|"nonstationary"|"stationary", "description": str}
  def generate(kind: str, duration_s: float, fs: int = 16000, rng: np.random.Generator | None = None, **params) -> np.ndarray  # float32 mono, finite, peak <= 0.99, exact length round(duration_s*fs)
Required kinds (randomize parameters per call so each call is a new instance):
 - gunshot_single: muzzle blast as Friedlander waveform p(t)=Ps(1-t/T+)exp(-b t/T+) with positive-phase durations ~0.5-3 ms, optional supersonic-projectile N-wave preceding it (~0.2-0.5 ms, arrives earlier for downrange observer), ground reflection (delayed, attenuated copy), distance-dependent air-absorption low-pass, reverberant/echo tail (exponentially decaying filtered noise, 0.2-1.5 s, outdoor/urban/indoor variants); random onset; background silence elsewhere (tiny noise floor).
 - gunfire_burst: automatic fire, 600-1000 rounds/min with jitter, bursts of 3-15 rounds, possibly several bursts.
 - gunfire_sporadic: several shooters at different distances (different spectra/levels), random times.
 - artillery: distant and near artillery/explosions: strong low-frequency content (< 200 Hz), longer positive phase (5-50 ms), rumble and long reverberant decay (1-4 s), optional incoming/outgoing whistle.
 - explosion: close blast + debris/crackle.
 - helicopter: main rotor blade-passing frequency 10-30 Hz with harmonics and impulsive blade-vortex-interaction "slap" pulses at BPF, tail rotor BPF 50-120 Hz harmonics, turbine whine tones 1-6 kHz, broadband aerodynamic noise, slow amplitude modulation; optional Doppler/fly-by.
 - drone_multirotor: 4-8 rotors each with own BPF 80-400 Hz (RPM jitter/drift, manoeuvre changes), 10-30 harmonics with decaying amplitude, motor electrical whine, broadband turbulence.
 - siren_wail (0.1-0.5 Hz sweep between ~600 and ~1500 Hz), siren_yelp (2-5 Hz sweep), siren_hilo (two-tone alternation ~1-2 Hz): harmonic-rich (square-ish), optional Doppler shift for a passing vehicle.
 - wind: gusty low-frequency turbulence on a microphone (spectrum concentrated < 500 Hz, gust envelope with 0.2-5 s fluctuations, occasional pop/rumble bursts); cite Nelke & Vary (2014) wind noise generation if you rely on it.
 - tracked_vehicle: diesel engine firing-frequency harmonics (20-80 Hz fundamental, many harmonics), track-slap periodic impulses, gearbox whine, broadband.
 - jet_flyby: broadband jet noise with Doppler, slow level envelope.
Each kind: document the physical basis and parameter ranges in docstrings (cite sources you are confident about, e.g. Maher 'Acoustical characterization of gunshots' 2007; Beck, Nakasone, Marr 'Variations in recorded acoustic gunshot waveforms...' 2011 if appropriate; mark anything uncertain). Must be reasonably fast (< 0.2 s to generate 10 s of any kind).
Also create ${ROOT}/scripts/plot_synth_noise.py which generates 6 s of each kind (fixed seed), saves wav files to ${ROOT}/data/synthetic_examples/<kind>.wav and spectrogram PNGs to ${ROOT}/reports/figures/synth_noise/<kind>.png plus a combined grid figure ${ROOT}/reports/figures/synth_noise_grid.png. Run it.
Create ${ROOT}/tests/test_synth_noise.py: lengths, finiteness, determinism given seed, different instances for different seeds, KINDS categories, impulsive kinds have high crest factor (peak/RMS), rotor/drone kinds show strong low-frequency harmonic peaks, siren energy concentrated in 500-3000 Hz band.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'baselines',
    prompt: `Create ${ROOT}/src/danc/models/baselines.py: classical single-channel speech-enhancement baselines, all CAUSAL (frame-by-frame, no look-ahead) and using danc.dsp STFT conventions (20 ms / 10 ms) so latency is comparable to the DNN.
API:
  def spectral_subtraction(x: np.ndarray, fs: int = 16000, alpha: float | None = None, beta: float = 0.02, **kw) -> np.ndarray   # Berouti/Schwartz/Makhoul 1979 over-subtraction with spectral floor (alpha SNR-dependent if None), Boll 1979
  def wiener_dd(x, fs=16000, **kw) -> np.ndarray   # Wiener gain with decision-directed a-priori SNR (Scalart & Vieira Filho 1996; Ephraim & Malah 1984 DD)
  def logmmse(x, fs=16000, **kw) -> np.ndarray     # Ephraim & Malah 1985 log-spectral amplitude estimator with DD a-priori SNR, gain floor
  def enhance(x, method: str, fs=16000, **kw) -> np.ndarray   # method in {"specsub","wiener","logmmse"}
  class NoiseTracker  # causal noise PSD estimator usable frame-by-frame: implement MCRA-2 (Rangachari & Loizou 2006) or IMCRA (Cohen 2003) or minimum statistics (Martin 2001) - pick one you can implement correctly, cite it, and expose update(power_frame)->noise_psd. Initialize from the first ~100-200 ms assuming noise-only, but keep tracking afterwards.
All functions return float32 arrays of the same length as x, finite, no NaN for silence or very loud impulses. Avoid musical-noise blowups (gain floor, smoothing).
Create ${ROOT}/tests/test_baselines.py using synthetic signals (e.g. a harmonic speech-like signal with on/off syllable envelope + white/pink noise at 0 dB): each method improves SNR measurably (> 3 dB for logmmse/wiener on stationary white noise), output length/dtype, robustness to silence and to a huge impulse, causality (output before time t unchanged if input after t changes).`,
  },
  {
    key: 'adaptive_dualmic',
    prompt: `Create two modules.
(1) ${ROOT}/src/danc/adaptive/nlms.py - reference-microphone adaptive noise cancellers (Widrow et al. 1975 'Adaptive noise cancelling: principles and applications', Proc. IEEE):
  class TimeNLMS: __init__(n_taps=64, mu=0.1, eps=1e-6, leak=0.0); process(primary_block, reference_block, mu_scale=1.0) -> error_block (streaming, keeps state across calls; numpy, reasonably vectorized/loop ok); reset().
  class SubbandNLMS: STFT-domain multi-frame complex NLMS operating on the shared danc.dsp STFT frames (so it adds ZERO extra latency when sharing analysis with the DNN). __init__(n_bins=161, n_taps=4, mu=0.3, beta=0.9 (power smoothing), delta=1e-4 (relative regularization), impulse_kappa=20.0, max_misadjust...); step(P: (F,) complex primary frame, R: (F,) complex reference frame, mu_scale: float | (F,) array in [0,1] = 1) -> E: (F,) complex. Per bin: Y = sum_k W[f,k]*R[t-k,f]; E = P - Y; W += mu*mu_scale * conj? (use correct complex NLMS: W[f,k] += mu * E * conj(R[t-k,f]) / (sum_k |R|^2 + delta*avgpower)). mu_scale is how an external speech-presence probability (from the DNN) freezes adaptation during speech (like double-talk control in AEC). Impulse robustness: if the instantaneous reference frame power exceeds impulse_kappa x its slow running average, skip (or strongly reduce) the update for that frame (still filter). Also guard against divergence (clip |W|, reset bin if non-finite).
  def run_subband_nlms(primary: np.ndarray, reference: np.ndarray, spp: np.ndarray | None = None, **kw) -> np.ndarray : offline helper using danc.dsp.stft/istft, frame loop; spp is (T,F) or (T,) speech-presence used as mu_scale = 1 - spp.
  def run_time_nlms(primary, reference, **kw) -> np.ndarray.
(2) ${ROOT}/src/danc/data/dual_mic.py - dual-microphone headset/helmet scene simulator for training/evaluating the hybrid (reference mic + DNN) system:
  @dataclass DualMicConfig: mic_spacing_m range (0.08-0.15), speech_leak_db range (-25..-12 dB speech level at reference relative to primary), n_directional range (1-3), source distance range (1-30 m), diffuse_ratio range (fraction of noise energy that is diffuse), self_noise_db (-70..-60 dBFS), c=343.
  def simulate_scene(speech: np.ndarray, noises: list[np.ndarray], snr_db: float, rng: np.random.Generator, cfg: DualMicConfig = DualMicConfig(), fs=16000) -> dict with keys primary, reference, clean (speech component at primary mic = training/eval target), noise_primary, noise_reference, meta (dict of sampled parameters). Directional noise sources: far-field plane waves or spherical with fractional-delay (windowed-sinc) propagation to the two mics plus 1-3 early reflections (ground/body) with random delay/attenuation, and a mild random relative transfer filter (short FIR) to mimic head/helmet shadowing; diffuse component with spherically-isotropic coherence Gamma(f)=sinc(2 pi f d / c) generated by mixing two independent noise realizations in the STFT domain (Habets & Gannot 2007 'Generating sensor signals in isotropic noise fields', JASA - cite) ; speech leakage into reference attenuated by speech_leak_db, delayed by d/c plus small FIR; mic self-noise uncorrelated. SNR is defined at the PRIMARY mic over the whole segment (speech energy / total noise energy). Inputs: noises list are mono noise signals (>= len(speech)), each assigned to a directional source or the diffuse field.
Create ${ROOT}/tests/test_adaptive.py: (a) TimeNLMS and SubbandNLMS cancel a purely coherent (delayed+filtered) noise by > 15 dB after convergence; (b) with speech present and mu_scale=0 during speech frames, speech is not cancelled (output speech component within 1 dB) while with mu_scale=1 and strong leakage the speech is partially cancelled (demonstrates why SPP control matters); (c) impulse robustness: a huge impulse in the reference does not make the filter diverge; (d) simulate_scene shapes/SNR at primary correct within 0.5 dB, diffuse noise inter-mic coherence approximately follows sinc(2 pi f d/c) (check a few bands loosely), determinism with seed.
Also create ${ROOT}/scripts/demo_nlms.py printing a small table of noise-reduction dB for coherent vs diffuse noise vs mic spacing (shows LMS only works for coherent noise; diffuse coherence falls above ~c/(2d)). Run it and include output in your summary.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'jetson_deploy',
    prompt: `Create the Jetson AGX Orin deployment kit under ${ROOT}/deploy/jetson/ (this machine is a Mac; you cannot run TensorRT here, so everything Jetson-specific must be clearly marked "NOT VERIFIED ON HARDWARE IN THIS PROJECT").
Model contract (will be produced by the main developer at ${ROOT}/exports/dancnet_stream.onnx): a stateful single-frame streaming network. Inputs: "spec" float32 [1,1,161,2] (real/imag of the current STFT frame), plus K state tensors named "state_in_0".."state_in_{K-1}" (float32, static shapes readable from the ONNX graph). Outputs: "spec_out" float32 [1,1,161,2] (enhanced frame), "spp" float32 [1,1,161] (speech presence 0..1, used to gate the reference-mic adaptive filter), and "state_out_0".."state_out_{K-1}" matching the input states. Frame hop = 10 ms (160 samples @16 kHz), window 20 ms, so per-frame compute must be << 10 ms.
Files to create:
 - deploy/jetson/README.md: complete bring-up guide for the NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 64GB Developer Kit: JetPack 6.x install notes, power modes (sudo nvpmodel -q / -m <id>, jetson_clocks), recommended mode for latency vs power, Python env (onnxruntime-gpu wheels for Jetson from the Jetson AI Lab / NVIDIA, TensorRT python bindings shipped with JetPack), how to build the TensorRT engine, how to run the real-time engine (python -m danc.inference.realtime --backend trt|ort ...), CPU-vs-GPU guidance for tiny batch-1 streaming models (kernel-launch overhead; consider ARM CPU via ONNX Runtime, or CUDA Graphs with TensorRT), audio hardware: (a) USB audio interface with 2 mic inputs (primary boom mic + outward-facing reference mic) and headphone out, (b) I2S MEMS mics on the 40-pin header (note device-tree/pinmux configuration via jetson-io is required), ALSA period/buffer sizing for low latency (e.g. 160-frame periods, 2-3 periods), PipeWire/JACK notes, real-time scheduling (chrt -f, isolcpus, performance governor), comm-unit/radio integration (line-out level matching, isolation transformer/ground loop, PTT keying via GPIO or radio accessory connector, sidetone path kept analog/unprocessed to avoid own-voice latency issues), latency measurement by electrical loopback (impulse/chirp in, cross-correlate), power measurement with tegrastats and the on-board INA3221 rails, thermal notes. A troubleshooting section. Mark unverified items.
 - deploy/jetson/build_trt_engine.sh: trtexec commands for FP32 and FP16 engines (static shapes from the ONNX, --saveEngine, --dumpProfile/--separateProfileRun, --useCudaGraph, timing log), with comments; INT8 noted as requiring calibration and quality re-validation.
 - deploy/jetson/trt_runner.py: TensorRT 10.x Python API runner class TRTStepRunner(engine_path) with reset() and __call__(spec: np.ndarray[1,1,161,2]) -> (spec_out, spp), discovering state tensors by name prefix, double-buffering states (swap in/out each frame), using pinned host buffers and either cuda-python (cudart) or torch CUDA tensors for device memory - document the dependency choice; optional CUDA graph capture. Include a __main__ micro-benchmark (N frames, mean/p50/p99 ms).
 - deploy/jetson/setup_audio.sh: list ALSA devices (arecord -l / aplay -l), example asound.conf for a 2-channel capture + stereo playback device, set CPU governor to performance, notes on disabling PulseAudio/PipeWire for the device or using pw-jack.
 - deploy/jetson/danc.service: systemd unit running the engine with real-time priority (LimitRTPRIO, CPUSchedulingPolicy=fifo), restart on failure.
 - deploy/jetson/log_power.sh: tegrastats logging to CSV with timestamps for N seconds while the engine runs; how to read VDD_GPU_SOC/VDD_CPU_CV/VIN_SYS_5V0 rails (names differ across JetPack versions - say so).
 - deploy/jetson/measure_latency.py: loopback latency measurement script using sounddevice: plays a chirp/MLS on output, records input, cross-correlates, reports round-trip latency; works on Mac too (for the I/O path only).
 - deploy/ALTERNATIVE_PLATFORMS.md: brief, clearly-hedged comparison of comparable targets (Jetson Orin NX/Nano, Qualcomm QCS6490/QCS8550, NXP i.MX 8M Plus NPU, TI AM62A/C7x DSP, ADI SHARC, Raspberry Pi 5 CPU) for this workload, stating that numbers must be checked against vendor datasheets (do not invent TOPS/power numbers you are not sure of; you may use WebSearch/WebFetch via ToolSearch "select:WebSearch,WebFetch" to verify vendor specs and cite URLs+dates).
Also create ${ROOT}/tests/test_jetson_scripts.py that at least byte-compiles trt_runner.py and measure_latency.py (py_compile) and checks build_trt_engine.sh / setup_audio.sh pass "bash -n". Verify the Jetson AGX Orin 64GB specs you quote (AI performance, CPU, GPU, power range, memory) against NVIDIA's official pages with WebFetch and cite URL+date in the README.`,
  },
]

const built = await pipeline(
  MODULES,
  m => agent(`${COMMON}\n\nYOUR MODULE: ${m.key}\n${m.prompt}`, { label: `build:${m.key}`, phase: 'Build' }),
  (summary, m) => agent(`${COMMON}\n\nYou are an ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER for the module "${m.key}" that another engineer just built. Its spec was:\n---\n${m.prompt}\n---\nBuilder's summary:\n${summary}\n\nRead every file it created. Look for: incorrect DSP math (complex NLMS conjugation, normalization, coherence formulas, Friedlander waveform, LSA gain formula, noise-tracker logic), non-causal processing where causality is required, NaN/inf risks, wrong units (dB vs linear, power vs amplitude), spec violations (API signatures, return types, lengths), tests that pass vacuously, fabricated or wrong citations, and for the Jetson kit any statement presented as verified that cannot be. FIX every real problem directly in those files (edit only that module's files; never delete files), re-run its tests until they pass, and return: list of issues found (severity, file:line, fix applied) and the final pytest summary line.`, { label: `review:${m.key}`, phase: 'Review' })
    .then(review => ({ module: m.key, build: summary, review })),
)
return built.filter(Boolean)
